lead: Jersey City plumbing deals with old brownstones, high-rise towers, lead lines and flooding. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Jersey City.
risk: old lead and galvanized pipes, basement flooding and stack leaks in multi-unit buildings
risk_short: old pipes, flooding and stack leaks
why: The Heights, Bergen-Lafayette and Downtown have row houses and brownstones from the 1800s and early 1900s, with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines in some cases.
Heavy storms, like Ida in 2021, flood basements and back up sewers in low areas. Newer towers near the waterfront share risers and booster pumps.
water: Jersey City's water comes mainly from the Boonton Reservoir. It is moderately soft. The utility has a lead service line replacement program.
tips: Ask JCMUA about your service line material.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Know where your unit's shutoff is.
Check building rules before plumbing work.
areas: PipeMend works Downtown and in Paulus Hook, the Heights, Journal Square, Greenville, Bergen-Lafayette, the West Side and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Jersey City Division of Construction Code, and plumbers must be licensed by the New Jersey State Board of Examiners of Master Plumbers.

faq.q: Who can do plumbing work in Jersey City?
faq.a: New Jersey requires a licensed master plumber for most plumbing work, and the city's construction code office issues permits. Ask for the license number before work starts.
